ports.name: clk_i
ports.functionality: Provides the rising edge that sequences all clocked assignments. It times updates to addr_ff, rdata, mem_ram_b*, rden and bus_rsp_o.ack in the mem_access and bus_feedback processes.
ports.evidence: rising_edge(clk_i) used in mem_access and bus_feedback processes that assign rdata, addr_ff, mem_ram_b*, rden and bus_rsp_o.ack

ports.name: rstn_i
ports.functionality: Provides asynchronous reset control for clocked logic. When '0' it forces rden and bus_rsp_o.ack to '0' in the bus_feedback process reset branch.
ports.evidence: if (rstn_i = '0') then ... in bus_feedback process assigns rden and bus_rsp_o.ack

ports.name: bus_req_i
ports.functionality: Conveys address, control and write-data fields into the entity. Its fields drive internal addr calculation, gate and supply RAM writes, and contribute to rden and ack generation.
ports.evidence: bus_req_i.* fields are read in addr assignment, mem_access write conditions, and bus_feedback rden/ack assignments

ports.name: bus_req_i.addr
ports.functionality: Supplies the high address bits which are sliced and converted to the internal word index 'addr'. The slice addr(addr_hi_c downto 2) forms addr used to index memory.

ports.name: bus_req_i.data
ports.functionality: Provides 32-bit write data for memory writes. Its byte slices (7..0,15..8,23..16,31..24) are written into mem_ram_b0..b3 when writes are enabled.
role: feeds RAM byte lanes during writes
ports.evidence: mem_ram_bX(to_integer(addr)) <= bus_req_i.data(<slice>) inside clocked mem_access process

ports.name: bus_req_i.ben
ports.functionality: Per-byte enable bits gate writes to the corresponding mem_ram_b* arrays. Each ben(i) is tested to decide whether that byte lane is written during a bus write.

ports.name: bus_req_i.stb
ports.functionality: Indicates a valid bus transfer. It gates RAM writes and is used to compute rden and bus_rsp_o.ack in bus_feedback.
role: used to compute response ack and read enable
ports.evidence: (bus_req_i.stb = '1') used in mem_access conditions and rden/ack assignments in bus_feedback

ports.name: bus_req_i.rw
ports.functionality: Distinguishes writes (rw='1') from reads. It gates RAM writes together with stb and is used (negated) to compute rden and bus_rsp_o.ack.
ports.evidence: (bus_req_i.rw = '1') used in mem_access and rden <= bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw)

ports.name: bus_rsp_o
ports.functionality: Collects response fields ack, data and err driven inside the entity. Its subfields are driven from internal rdata/rden and from bus_feedback logic.
ports.evidence: bus_rsp_o.ack, bus_rsp_o.data and bus_rsp_o.err are assigned inside this entity

ports.name: bus_rsp_o.ack
ports.functionality: Registered output set in bus_feedback from bus_req_i.stb and bus_req_i.rw (and IMEM_INIT). Reports acknowledgement to the bus; updated on clk_i with rstn_i reset.
ports.evidence: Assigned in bus_feedback: bus_rsp_o.ack <= bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw) or bus_req_i.stb (IMEM_INIT dependent)

ports.name: bus_rsp_o.err
ports.functionality: Error output is driven constant '0' indicating no error from this memory implementation.
ports.evidence: Concurrent assignment bus_rsp_o.err <= '0' ties this port to constant '0'

ports.name: bus_rsp_o.data
ports.functionality: Combinationally driven from internal rdata when rden is '1', otherwise zeros. Exports the read word to the bus master.

signals.name: rdata
signals.functionality: Holds a 32-bit word read from ROM or assembled from the four RAM byte arrays. It is used as the source for bus_rsp_o.data when rden is asserted.
role: loaded from ROM or RAM arrays
signals.evidence: rdata <= mem_rom_c(...) or rdata(<slices>) <= mem_ram_bX(... ) in mem_access processes; bus_rsp_o.data reads rdata

signals.name: rden
signals.functionality: Registered flag set each clock to indicate a read transfer (bus_req_i.stb and not bus_req_i.rw). It gates whether rdata is presented on bus_rsp_o.data.
signals.evidence: rden <= bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw) in bus_feedback (clocked); used in bus_rsp_o.data conditional

signals.name: addr
signals.functionality: Combinationally derived from bus_req_i.addr slice (addr_hi_c downto 2) and used as the word index to address ROM/RAM and to feed addr_ff.
signals.evidence: addr <= unsigned(bus_req_i.addr(addr_hi_c downto 2)); addr used as index to mem_ram_bX(...) and mem_rom_c(...)

signals.name: addr_ff
signals.functionality: Captures addr on clock edges in the alternative access style and provides a stable index for ROM/RAM reads (used by concurrent reads in alt style).
role: addresses memory when alternative style used
signals.evidence: addr_ff <= addr in alt_style mem_access processes; addr_ff used in mem_ram_bX(to_integer(addr_ff)) and mem_rom_c(to_integer(addr_ff)) reads

signals.name: mem_ram_b0
signals.functionality: Stores low byte per word address. Written on clocked writes from bus_req_i.data(7 downto 0) when stb,rw and ben(0) allow; read to form rdata(7 downto 0).
signals.evidence: mem_ram_b0(to_integer(addr)) <= bus_req_i.data(7 downto 0) inside rising_edge guard; rdata(7 downto 0) <= mem_ram_b0(to_integer(addr))

signals.name: mem_ram_b1
signals.functionality: Stores second byte per word address. Written from bus_req_i.data(15 downto 8) when enabled; read to form rdata(15 downto 8).
signals.evidence: mem_ram_b1(to_integer(addr)) <= bus_req_i.data(15 downto 8) inside rising_edge guard; rdata(15 downto 8) <= mem_ram_b1(to_integer(addr))

signals.name: mem_ram_b2
signals.functionality: Stores third byte per word address. Written from bus_req_i.data(23 downto 16) when enabled; read to form rdata(23 downto 16).
signals.evidence: mem_ram_b2(to_integer(addr)) <= bus_req_i.data(23 downto 16) inside rising_edge guard; rdata(23 downto 16) <= mem_ram_b2(to_integer(addr))

signals.name: mem_ram_b3
signals.functionality: Stores high byte per word address. Written from bus_req_i.data(31 downto 24) when enabled; read to form rdata(31 downto 24).
signals.evidence: mem_ram_b3(to_integer(addr)) <= bus_req_i.data(31 downto 24) inside rising_edge guard; rdata(31 downto 24) <= mem_ram_b3(to_integer(addr))
